STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall shadow).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are 20-30 cm; this one looks medium-large, around 23-25 cm.
b) Reference: the blueberries are about 1.5 cm across, and the strawberries run roughly 3-4 cm. The plate spans roughly 7-8 strawberry-lengths across the width, which gives about 24 cm (taking strawberry ~3.2 cm).
Reconciled width: 24 cm, area about 576 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items (small, flat layer, no mound):
- Pineapple chunks: about 10 visible pieces, roughly 2 cm cubes, one or two layers. Footprint about 8% of plate, ~46 cm². Thickness about 1.5 cm average (chunks sit about 2 cm thick). Volume ~69 ml x 0.6 = ~41 g.
- Strawberries: about 6 whole/halved berries, footprint about 10% (~58 cm²), average thickness about 2 cm (berries stacked to ~3 cm at the centre). Volume ~116 ml x 0.6 = ~70 g.
- Blueberries: about 12 berries, each 1.5 cm, footprint ~1.5% (~9 cm²), thickness ~1.5 cm. Count 12 x ~1.0 g ≈ 12 g (blueberry about 1.2 g each, so ~14 g; use 14 g).

Hidden food: no base layer; the plate centre is empty, so no hidden items.

STEP 4 - Total weight: 41 + 70 + 14 = about 125 g.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (fresh fruit):
- Pineapple: 50 kcal/100 g
- Strawberry: 32 kcal/100 g
- Blueberry: 57 kcal/100 g

Energy: pineapple 41 g ≈ 20 kcal; strawberries 70 g ≈ 22 kcal; blueberries 14 g ≈ 8 kcal. Total ≈ 50 kcal.
